Curious if this is possible. Currently working on a database at work to keep track of our Temp Workers and pertinent info. In the main table "tblTempWorker" I have a yes/no field "fHired" that keeps track of whether or not the temp was hired. At the moment I'm building a simple query in order to keep the general stats of our temp workers,i.e. avg number of days employed and what not. Would like to have a field in that query that would show me the percentage of temp workers who were hired in. In other words, if I had 100 temp workers and 50 were hired, as marked by my yes/no field, the field I would build in the query would display 50%

Any help or ideas would be greatly appreciated.
Turning a "yes/no" field into a percentage

If you are keeping averages already then I assume this is a totals query. As part of the aggregate, add a count for a field that will be populated (like the primary key). Secondly add a sum of the true\false variable. True false variables are stored as 0 (false) and -1 (true). So in the third column you simply do the math. To refer to a filed already in an aggregate query you call it FxnOfVariableName. So you would have 

qPrcnt = (SumOfWasHired/CountOfPrimaryKey)*-1

Good luck

Alright I got it and here's what I did. In my query I set up a new calculated field to add up the yes's and used the absolute function to get that to a positive 'fHiredCount: Abs(Sum([fHired])). Then set up another calculated field to add up all the Temp Workers I have on the table 'fTotalCount: Count([ID]). After that, I set up my final calculated field to get my percentage "fPercentage: Abs(([fHiredCount]/[fTotalCount])*100)"
